subject: LedgerOne reserved throughput shortfall — legal/SLA flag
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha@ledgerone.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carlson <ben.carlson@ledgerone.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production latency + error spike on our reserved pool — urgent

David —

We're seeing a sustained degradation in throughput on our reserved capacity for the last ~30 minutes. p99 generation latency for our main payment routing model has jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s; 5xx rate has spiked to 4.6% (previously <0.1%). This is causing transaction timeouts in our processing pipeline and customers are reporting failed authorizations.

Ben and I are on standby. We need immediate mitigation and a clear ETA for full restoration. Our contract (LDG-3821) has a 99.9% uptime SLA and this window is already impacting merchant SLAs.

Attached: throughput_digests_20270515.pdf (sample spans, request ids).

Please advise next steps and whether you can temporarily route us to an alternate model or capacity while you investigate. We need an executive contact for escalation.

—Asha
Lead Integrations Manager
LedgerOne
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha@ledgerone.com>
Cc: Ben Carlson <ben.carlson@ledgerone.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-15T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency + error spike on our reserved pool — urgent

Asha — thanks for the heads up and the sample file. We're investigating now; I've looped in ops (Marissa) and infra (Jonas). Immediate plan: 1) isolate the affected model variant and throttle traffic to it, 2) provision a temporary burst node from Dedicated pool if autoscale doesn't kick, 3) offer a routing fallback to the compatible hosted variant.

Can you confirm whether you want us to automatically fail traffic to the hosted variant (we can do a transparent redirect) or prefer a maintenance window? Also: do you authorize Redwood to upload debug traces for joint inspection?

I'll post status updates in this thread every 30 minutes until service is stable. Executive contact: David Kim (I will escalate internally to our CTO and VP Sales if needed).

-David
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Rao <asha@ledgerone.com>, Ben Carlson <ben.carlson@ledgerone.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Ops findings — reserved pool utilization + model tail latency

Team / Asha — quick summary of what ops is seeing:
- Reserved GPU pool (pool-id: ded-ldg-003) is pegged at 98% util for the last 22 minutes.
- Queue depth increased from baseline 12 -> 97; per-instance KV cache hit rate dropped 6% which raised effective decoder work.
- Root cause signal: a recent model variant (v3b-compat) rolled out in the customer's route increases token decode cost by ~3x for the common prompt patterns. The variant was supposed to be backward-compatible but introduced extra attention layers in the compiled graph.

Immediate actions taken:
- Throttled v3b-compat for LedgerOne to 20% of prior traffic.
- Enabled fallback routing to hosted model 'redwood-compat-1' for high-priority routes (transaction_auth).
- Opened capacity burst request (pending quota approval).

Next steps for full remediation:
1) Revert v3b-compat rollout for LedgerOne (25m ops work).
2) If quota approve, add 1x burst machine for 2 hours.
3) Deep kernel trace to confirm why v3b increases decode cost; offline code fix required.

I'll keep Asha updated. If legal is sensitive to SLA windows, we should prepare credit numbers and the audit logs. Attached: audit_log_excerpt.txt (ops extract).

-Marissa
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Rao <asha@ledgerone.com>
Date: 2027-05-15T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Ops findings — routing change deployed, capacity request submitted

Quick update: routing change to redirect transaction_auth traffic to redwood-compat-1 is live (09:58 PDT). Observed immediate drop in 5xxs from 4.6% -> 0.9% on the route, and p99 latency on the fallback model is ~180ms.

I've submitted a manual quota-burst for pool ded-ldg-003 (request #QB-20270515-11) to add one gtx128 node for 3 hours; finance approval path indicates we can cover an emergency burst under customer-impact clause but need sign-off from Sales / Revenue Ops for billing adjustments.

Attached: sla_impact_summary.xlsx (calculated downtime window and estimated customer exposures).

-Jonas
Lead Infra Eng
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha@ledgerone.com>, Ben Carlson <ben.carlson@ledgerone.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency + error spike on our reserved pool — urgent (status & offer)

Asha / Ben —

Thanks for your patience. Summary of actions taken so far:
- Routed transaction_auth traffic to redwood-compat-1 (reduced error rate and latency).
- Throttled the problematic v3b-compat variant to minimize tail decode cost.
- Submitted emergency capacity burst request (QB-20270515-11).
- Ops captured audit excerpts and perf digests.

We will:
- Keep the fallback routing in place until we fully validate a safe rollout path for v3b-compat.
- Offer LedgerOne a one-time service credit equivalent to 8 hours at committed throughput rate for the SLA window while we complete remediation — we are prepared to discuss the exact credit and process.

Can we schedule a short executive call today (30m) to walk through root cause and next steps? Jonas and Marissa will join. Please propose a time; I can escalate to our CTO if LedgerOne wants exec-level commitment.

-David
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Asha Rao <asha@ledgerone.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carlson <ben.carlson@ledgerone.com>
Cc: LedgerOne Legal <legal@ledgerone.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-15T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency + error spike on our reserved pool — urgent

David — thanks for the rapid mitigation. We can confirm that routing to redwood-compat-1 reduced failed authorizations immediately. However, this incident is a material SLA deviation under section 5.2 of LDG-3821. We're copying LedgerOne Legal; they will open a formal SLA claim.

We need the following by COB tomorrow (May 16):
1) Full RCA with kernel traces and timeline.
2) Confirmed remediation plan and expected date for safe re-rollout of v3b-compat.
3) Proposed credit calculation and how it will be applied.

Legal has asked us to preserve all logs and communications.

—Asha
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Asha Rao <asha@ledgerone.com>, Ben Carlson <ben.carlson@ledgerone.com>, LedgerOne Legal <legal@ledgerone.com>
Date: 2027-05-17T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: LedgerOne SLA claim — internal action & exec ask

Forwarding customer legal notice and thread. Key asks for leadership:
- Approve one-time credit: recommend approving the 8-hour committed-rate credit offered to LedgerOne to expedite closure.
- Approve emergency capacity spend (QB-20270515-11) for 3 hours while ops completes the kernel diagnostic (cost estimate attached to Jira INF-9876).
- Comms approval: we need a joint Exec->Customer note (CTO + Head of Sales) confirming timelines and remedial steps by EOD tomorrow.

Ops update: Marissa has the kernel traces and is drafting the RCA. Preliminary root cause: variant v3b-compat introduced an unexpected compiled attention pattern that increases decode work for ~18% of LedgerOne request shapes — patch required in the compile pipeline.

Please reply with approve/deny for the credit and emergency burst so I can respond to Legal and LedgerOne.

-David
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
